before every fashion house wanted to be a tech company, Prada made a phone with LG.

the Prada Phone by LG arrived in 2007: glossy black, ultra-minimal and almost entirely touchscreen. and the slightly insane part? it was the first commercially released phone with a capacitive touchscreen, landing in stores before the original iPhone. today, fashion lost one of the people who helped make the industry what it is behind the scenes.

Mathilde Favier, Dior’s longtime PR director, has passed away, aged 57 following an accident in France. for more than a decade at Dior, she was one of the invisible forces connecting the house with the people, celebrities and cultural moments that made it feel larger than fashion.

introducing our new series, “fashion by film”, where we look back at the movies that made their way from the screen onto the runway.

Dion Lee deserved a different ending.

for 15 years, Dion Lee built one of those rare fashion languages you could recognise without ever seeing the label: technical construction, corsetry, cut-outs, hardware and clothes that somehow felt futuristic, architectural and extremely sexy all at once.

founded in Sydney in 2009, the brand went from Australian Fashion Week to New York, dressing everyone from Rosalía to Zendaya and Taylor Swift and becoming one of Australia’s biggest global fashion exports.

then, almost unbelievably, it unravelled. after long-time investor Cue withdrew its backing, the Australian business entered voluntary administration in May 2024 with liabilities later estimated at more than AUD $35 million. no acceptable buyer was found, and by August the companies behind the label were voted into liquidation.

a very abrupt ending for a brand that had such a ridiculously strong point of view.

we miss Dion Lee. a lot.

the more you look at Maison Margiela’s Fall 2018 Artisanal collection, the more it feels like Galliano was designing for a world that hadn’t happened yet.

clothes crushed, layered and repurposed. sleeping bags and removal blankets turned into couture. phones strapped to ankles filming the front row, iPads built into bags and VR headsets styled as accessories. Galliano called it “nomadic glamour”, dressing for people carrying their entire world with them.

eight years later, with tech basically attached to us and fashion increasingly obsessed with protection, layering and making something new from what already exists… this feels less like an archive and more like a prediction.

Jonathan Anderson’s Dior Cigale quickly became the bag of the moment.

sometimes, the most meaningful luxury isn’t meant to be seen.

designer Ambie Stapleton spent months secretly creating Brenda’s engagement ring alongside her now-fiancé Isaac.

the result? a recycled platinum ring with every diamond hidden on the inside, a detail only the couple will ever truly see. inspired by the windows of New York’s iconic Seagram Building, the pattern transforms 14 princess-cut and 14 baguette diamonds into a private symbol of their relationship rather than a public display.

the most beautiful things aren’t always the ones asking to be noticed.
